rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a multimodal setup with advanced RNA (scgpt) and image (imagenet_vit_l) encoders, which are likely to capture complex patterns. Weighted fusion may improve performance compared to simple concatenation. This balances exploration of high-impact design choices (advanced encoders) with a reasonable cost estimate.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with weighted fusion (like config_003) achieve 0.422 validation accuracy. This experiment tests a similar setup but with simpler encoders (pca_n2000 and resnet50) to reduce training cost while maintaining the weighted fusion strategy. It clarifies whether encoder choices impact accuracy without increasing GPU hours, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows config_005 (singleprofile) achieves 0.523 accuracy with resnet50 and pca_n2000. Testing config_009 (multiprofile) with the same RNA encoder but larger imagenet_vit_l image encoder could improve accuracy by leveraging stronger image features. This clarifies whether multiprofile settings outperform singleprofile, while using a more powerful image encoder. Expected cost is higher than config_005 but justified by potential accuracy gains.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile multimodal models with scgpt RNA encoder and weighted fusion (like config_009) achieve high accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests whether using resnet50 image encoder (instead of imagenet_vit_l) with avgpool aggregation maintains similar performance at lower cost. It clarifies if the image encoder choice impacts accuracy while keeping training cost manageable (estimated ~5 GPU hours). This balances exploitation of proven components (scgpt, weighted fusion) with exploration of a cheaper image encoder.

The existing evidence shows config_009 (multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.635). This experiment tests changing the fusion method to 'concat' while keeping other parameters the same, which could clarify if fusion type impacts performance. It is a low-cost (similar to config_009's 7.02 GPU hours) exploration of a promising configuration space, balancing exploitation of current best practices with minor variation to reduce uncertainty.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with pca_n2000 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders (config_009) achieve the highest accuracy (0.635) so far. This experiment tests scgpt RNA with the same image encoder and aggregation method, clarifying if RNA encoder choice is critical. It balances exploration (testing a different RNA encoder) and exploitation (using proven image and aggregation choices), while keeping costs manageable (estimated ~4.5-6.0 GPU hours).

The existing evidence shows config_009 (pca_n2000 RNA, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests scgpt RNA with concat fusion, exploring whether a more complex RNA encoder paired with concat fusion could improve accuracy. It clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choice and fusion method. While expected to be slightly more expensive than config_009 (approx 7.5 GPU hours), it balances exploration of promising components (scgpt) with cost efficiency.

Existing evidence shows config_009 (multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with weighted fusion on the same encoder combination, which could improve performance while maintaining reasonable cost. Transformer aggregation may capture more complex interactions than avgpool, and the expected cost (similar to config_009's 7.02 GPU hours) is manageable within the remaining budget.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups with pca_n2000 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image, using avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_009) achieve the highest accuracy of 0.635. Testing config_039, which uses scgpt RNA (potentially more powerful) with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, could improve accuracy. The expected cost is higher than config_009 (7.02 GPU hours), but it's the last experiment, so it's worth testing to see if it can surpass the current best.

The existing evidence shows config_009 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with the same RNA/image encoders but concat fusion, which could potentially improve accuracy by leveraging more complex interactions. Transformer aggregation is computationally more expensive (estimated 4.54 GPU hours) but may outperform avgpool. This balances exploration of aggregation methods with the goal of maximizing accuracy before the budget ends.
